Government was a lot smaller, and perhaps even more importantly it wasn't so controlled by corporations. The same corporations benefiting from our dysfunctional government are the ones who own the media. Just one corporation, Time Warner, owns CNN, HBO (Bill Maher, John Oliver, etc), TNT, TBS, DC Comics, Warner Bros Pictures, New Line Cinema, Castle Rock Entertainment, Cartoon Network, Cinemax, and literally hundreds of other major outlets and assets. In my opinion I think a big player here is that the government has been taken over by corporations. In some cases literally but more often simply in influence. The only thing that correlates strongly with political success in the US is money. Politicians spend more time raising money for their next election cycle than anything else. The mega corporations are the entities that can throw millions about like its pocket change. Put two and two together and politicians are suddenly bending over backwards to satisfy every whim of every corporation.

This is a complex issue because smaller governments are easier to easier to control than bigger governments. People love to hate on the EU because of their immigration stance, but they're actually one of the few governing bodies that has done a lot of good for the common people. For instance the EU ruled in 2010 that licenses don't override first sale doctrine even if they claim to do so. You'd never see a ruling like that in the US. In fact a similar case did come up in the US, Vernor vs Autodesk. The ruling is what you'd expect. First sale doctrine doesn't apply when corporations don't want it to in the US. The supreme court then refused to hear the case.

The EU is very large perhaps even more importantly it's controlled by a very vast group of member states who in turn are also large and have regularly rotating political control thanks to proportional representation. Taking that over is not particularly realistic. On the other hand should England actually secede not only from the EU but the UK as well, it's going to be a playground owned by multinational corporations - more than it already is - within 2 decades.
